title: Choose the console's visual world
question: The roll assigned The Supply Catalogue, translated to dark (you pinned dark-only). Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Supply Catalogue
options.lineage: Industrial supply catalogues: dense spec tables, family tabs, line-art parts
options.thesis: Every quote reads like a catalogue page: specs in tight tables, the moved figure tabbed in its material family's colour.
options.viewport: Owner strip of four figures on top; a left rail of material-family tabs (Elastomer, Filler, Metal); the work area is a dense spec table of the quotes a change hits. Cream catalogue stock is translated to graphite for the pinned dark theme.
options.risk: Dense tables tip into spreadsheet drudgery if the family tab colours are timid.

raised.raise: Every headline figure names the row it came from: each claim sits beside its proof.
All margin bars share one fixed scale, so cards compare at a glance down the column.
Focus mode: one card owns the work area and the next is one keystroke (J) away.
One what-if control (cost change %) reflows every affected margin live.

options.label: The Redline Blueprint
options.lineage: Cyanotype customer drawings with engineers' redline revisions
options.thesis: Quotes as drawings under revision: every cost change is a redline, every restated card a new Rev letter.
options.viewport: Standard top bar and lanes; each card closes in a title block (quote, customer, Rev B); changed figures are struck through and redlined.
options.risk: Blueprint is what most engineering products reach for first; it lands familiar.

options.label: Cost Line Map
options.thesis: A supplier change runs as a coloured line through materials to every quote it stops at; interchanges are quotes hit twice.
options.viewport: Top bar and queue; above the queue a line diagram from supplier email to material to affected quotes, rings marking stacked changes.
options.case: Wins clarity (the one-email-to-many-quotes cascade reads at once) but job shops don't live in transit maps.
options.risk: The diagram competes with the queue for the first glance.

options.label: Carbon-copy Coupons
options.lineage: Jet-age ticket wallets and multi-part carbon forms
options.thesis: Each card is a coupon in a quote book: approved stamps VALID, superseded stamps VOID; nothing disappears, it cancels.
materials: carbon numerals in ruled fare boxes
options.viewport: Queue of coupons on a navy ground; figures in carbon-purple numerals in ruled boxes; state stamps across each corner.
options.case: Wins audience (shops still run on carbon forms; stamps match the audit trail) but light coupons fight the pinned dark.
options.risk: Light coupons on a dark page make a contrast jump on every row.

options.label: Claim and Proof
options.thesis: One neutral scale, one accent, every claim beside the screenshot that proves it.
options.case: Fuses into the category default: loses audience and adds no clarity the console lacks.
options.risk: Indistinguishable from any dark SaaS dashboard.
options.kept: Every figure paired with its proof row.

options.label: Seasonal Folio
options.thesis: A quote's margin shown stage by stage on fixed-scale plates.
options.viewport: Quoted, change, after, revised as five aligned plates.
options.case: Loses both: foreign to shops and slower to read than a table.
options.risk: Reads as a book, not a tool.
options.kept: One fixed scale across every margin bar.

options.label: One at a Time
options.thesis: One card fills the screen; the next is one snap away.
options.viewport: A single decision card owns the viewport.
options.case: Loses both: estimators compare cards, and a feed hides the queue.
options.risk: Hides the size of the queue.
options.kept: A focus mode with the next card one keystroke away.

options.label: Live Specimen
options.thesis: One axis slider morphs the whole grid live.
options.viewport: A slider driving every figure on the page.
options.case: Loses both as a world; its one-control discipline transfers.
options.risk: A type showcase, not a work surface.
options.kept: One what-if control that reflows every margin.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A well-made dark B2B dashboard: neutral greys, one blue accent, cards and tables.
canonCard.viewport: Top bar, KPI row, tabbed queue, at full craft.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
